questions.question: The structural hallmark of a G-protein coupled receptor (GPCR) is:

options.A: A single transmembrane helix linked to an intracellular tyrosine kinase domain
options.B: Seven membrane-spanning helical segments with the agonist binding site on the extracellular face
options.C: A pentameric ring of subunits directly enclosing an ion channel
options.D: A soluble intracellular protein that binds directly to DNA

questions.explanation: GPCRs share a common structural motif: 7 alpha-helical membrane-spanning segments forming 3 extracellular and 3 intracellular loops, with the agonist binding site located between the helices on the extracellular face and the G-protein binding site on the cytosolic side.
questions.sourceBook: KD Tripathi, Essentials of Medical Pharmacology
questions.sourceChapter: Mechanism of Drug Action; Receptor Pharmacology
questions.subject: Pharmacology

questions.question: At the elbow, the radial collateral ligament mainly prevents excessive ______ and the ulnar collateral ligament mainly prevents excessive ______.
questions.explanation: The lateral (radial) collateral ligament resists varus stress and the medial (ulnar) collateral ligament resists valgus stress.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: The release of which hormones is controlled by the anterior pituitary?

questions.question: A therapist measures a patient's shoulder medial rotation with patient positioned in supine with glenohumeral joint in 90 degrees of abduction and the elbow in 90 degrees of flexion. The therapist records the patient's shoulder medial rotation is 0-70 degrees and classifies the end-feel as firm. Which portion of the joint capsule is primarily responsible for the firm end-feel?
